[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]
== Biography ==
'''William Glasgow''' of Killycurragh, County Tyrone, is named as the paternal grandfather in the undated family letter preserved as PRONI T1959/3. It reports his marriage to an unidentified Miss Cunningham of Omagh, five sons and three daughters, and sons James and Samuel who remained on the family farm.<ref name="FamilyLetter">Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, T1959/3, photocopy of an undated and unsigned family letter among papers of the 1890s; Albert Rutherford transcription reproduced by Gary Harding, [https://www.genealogy.com/forum/surnames/topics/rutherford/5445/ Rutherfords and Glasgows in Co. Tyrone, Ireland], 9 January 2005. Earlier reviewed account reused on 20 October 2026; original uninspected, online transcription unavailable (HTTP 403) at recheck.</ref>

His birth, death and birthplace are unknown. The letter reports his father as an older William of Killycurragh; the selected Scottish profile candidate is possible, 36%. The reported parental home was Killycurragh; no exact property or life dates are inferred. The family’s 1796 ministerial generation establishes historical context, not a recorded date for William.<ref>[https://cotyrone.com/churchrecord/ministers-pres.html Presbyterian Ministers in Co. Tyrone], John Glasgow from Orritor, ordained New Row 8 March 1796, died 13 July 1801; derivative compilation.</ref>

== Research Notes ==

=== Killycurragh generations, 20 October 2026 ===

The freshly read published transcription of PRONI T1959/3 distinguishes an older William of Killycurragh, the writer’s paternal great-grandfather, from his son William, the writer’s paternal grandfather and husband of Miss Cunningham. The younger William is the Cunningham husband, whose sons included James and Samuel. His son John married Margaret Glasgow after ordination at Coleraine and died at his father’s house in Orritor in July 1801. The surviving child, the anonymous writer, was born five months later; Margaret died in 1817. The separate church compilation identifies John Glasgow from Orritor, ordained at New Row, Coleraine, on 8 March 1796 and dead on 13 July 1801. The shared ministry, origin, name and death month strongly identify the husband. The writer separately describes Margaret’s father William as a son of James Glasgow and Margaret Rutherford; the two parental lines must not be collapsed into one grandfather.

Select [[Glasgow-1318|William Glasgow]] as the possible father of the letter-defined Cunningham husband at 36%. The letter supplies an older Killycurragh William, son of the Tullycoll/Tullyall William and brother of James (husband of Margaret Rutherford) and John (husband of Anne Mason). The 1705 Kirknewton child William has a named father William and a generation compatible with being grandfather of the minister ordained in 1796. The 1702 John baptism supplies a compatible second named son in that Scottish father cluster; the existing James-1025 family supplies the Irish James comparison. This is a positive but non-exclusive family-cluster hypothesis. The Scottish child’s adult identity and migration remain unproved. The 36% includes that identity uncertainty; it is not a confident Scottish–Irish bridge.

Select the letter-defined William of Killycurragh as Rev. John Glasgow’s father at 94% (strongly supported). The writer explicitly gives the writer’s father John, the writer’s paternal grandfather William and his Cunningham marriage. John’s Coleraine ordination, Orritor origin and July 1801 death match the separate New Row minister entry. This concerns the minister’s record-defined identity; it does not identify his grandfather with a Scottish baptism or upgrade his brothers’ later-profile matches.

Select [[Glasgow-2426|William Glasgow]] as Margaret Glasgow’s probable father at 84%. That profile represents William, son of [[Glasgow-1025|James Glasgow]] and Margaret Rutherford, which matches the letter’s maternal-grandfather family position. The letter explicitly names the eldest daughter Margaret as the minister’s wife and the writer’s mother. The profile’s circa-1735 birth and circa-1829 United States death are inherited claims, not exclusionary records and not corrected here. The letter calls William an eldest son; the circa-1735 estimate conflicts with the earlier estimated births of his attached brothers. Those unverified estimates require checking and are preserved here. This is the maternal grandfather, distinct from the Cunningham husband. Original records and an independent adult-life bridge remain to be found.

These are exact subjective assessments of complete relationship-and-identity propositions, not measured probabilities. The family letter is undated and unsigned and is read through Albert Rutherford’s published transcription of a photocopy, not an inspected PRONI original. The minister list is a derivative compilation whose independence from the family tradition is unproved. The Scottish adult identities remain possible: neither the letter nor the 1705 baptism supplies a migration, occupation, property or witness bridge between Kirknewton and Tyrone. The letter’s three-son family and second-cousin statement are internally consistent clues from one source, not independent corroborations. Existing people, vital fields and mothers are preserved. Miss Cunningham and Anne Rutherford are reported maternal names, not transferred to existing maternal profiles. The letter’s first-settler story is family tradition, not proof of the first Glasgow in Tyrone or of the surname’s origin.<ref name="KillycurraghGenerations20261020">PRONI T1959/3, [https://www.genealogy.com/forum/surnames/topics/rutherford/5445/ published transcription], read 20 October 2026; original uninspected. [https://cotyrone.com/churchrecord/ministers-pres.html Minister compilation], John Glasgow, New Row; derivative entry, not an original register.</ref>


Prefer the William named in PRONI T1959/3 as James Glasgow-4145’s probable working father, at 82% confidence. The letter’s paternal uncle James lived and died on the Killycurragh farm, matching the name, specific locality, generation and deceased status of the probate subject indexed at Killycarragh on 21 March 1836. The letter supplies the parent relationship absent from that index. The whole match remains inferred because the original probate document is lost and the letter is derivative; another local James remains possible.<ref name="FamilyLetter" />

Prefer the William named in PRONI T1959/3 as Samuel Glasgow-1698’s probable working father, at 66% confidence. The positive case combines the expressly named Samuel in the letter, the exact Killycurragh family-farm setting, and the later Samuel’s documented farmer/probate household there in 1857. It replaces an unnecessary blanket hold with a testable family placement. The identity is less secure than James’s: there is no traced lease succession or age for the letter’s Samuel, and the current birth estimate may represent a later generation.<ref name="FamilyLetter" />

The percentages assess each entire father-to-profile proposition, including identification of the named son with the later profile; they are subjective comparative judgments, not measured frequencies. The original letter and holding succession remain unverified. Samuel’s circa-1800 birth is an estimate, and a materially older Samuel or a later same-name descendant is possible. His wife Anne’s approximate 1801 birth and their children in the 1820s–1830s do not date Samuel himself. A nephew or later tenant could share the name and townland. Do not transfer a recorded relationship to a later adult merely from the letter’s parent clause. William’s birth and death remain unknown; his named father’s Scottish profile identity is now possible at 36%, and his mother is unidentified. Miss Cunningham is retained as William’s reported wife, without selecting her as either profile’s mother. No existing person is merged or redated, and no live WikiTree edit has been made.

Identity remains unresolved before creating a separate WikiTree profile. This is a documentary account for the working family, not a conclusion that William is a new unique person.

[[Glasgow-2426]] — The current James/Margaret Rutherford parentage instead fits the letter’s maternal grandfather; selected as Margaret’s probable father at 84%. Do not collapse the two grandfathers. This remains an alternative for the paternal grandfather only if that profile’s family placement is wrong.

[[Glasgow-2915]] — Compatible Cookstown-area father generation if the estimated 1760 birth is earlier. His reported wife Margaret Mitchell differs from Miss Cunningham; a prior marriage is possible but unproved. Missing family fields are not an exclusion. No selected identity or ancestral transfer follows.

Inspect PRONI T1959/3 and associated family papers; test William’s identity against existing candidates and trace the Killycurragh holding through leases, rentals and valuation revisions. Establish Samuel’s age independently. The 1836 index date is probate information, not James’s exact death date.

[https://glasgow.phenotype.dev/free-space/glasgow-of-killycurragh-early-c19-aa9477/ Killycurragh household study and current family discussion].
